attributes.question: Does a participant release reach users only after a centrally owned pointer or artifact (import map entry, environment pointer, router config, version pin) is updated, rather than the participant's own deploy alone going live?
attributes.notes: Host- or platform-controlled vs participant-controlled go-live. Yes: import-map architectures, single-spa, Zephyr environments. No: same-URL strategies (iframe, qiankun, wujie, micro-app, hyperfrontend, Podium, fragments). Conditional: OpenComponents (range consumers get it immediately, pinned consumers do not). Pairs with consumer-version-pin as the two directions of version control.

attributes.question: Can the host or consumer pin an exact participant version and keep receiving it regardless of newer participant deploys?
attributes.notes: Yes: OpenComponents exact pin, import maps (versioned URLs), Zephyr per-environment override, Bit (npm versions). No: same-URL strategies (the host receives whatever is deployed behind the URL). Conditional: MF (URL pinning by convention), Piral (feed decides).

attributes.question: Can a specific user, session, or preview audience be served a different participant version while production users keep the current one, via a first-party mechanism or documented pattern?
attributes.notes: Covers canary, preview, staged rollout. Yes: Piral feed (per-user, feature-flagged pilet sets), Zephyr (per-version preview URLs, per-environment overrides), Vercel platform (preview and branch routing). Conditional: import maps (import-map-overrides tooling, common-pattern). No or Unknown: Podium, qiankun, wujie, raw iframes (nothing documented). Score mechanism presence, not marketing.

attributes.question: Does a first-party mechanism keep every published participant version immutable and permanently addressable (duplicate name+version publish rejected, prior versions retained)?
attributes.notes: Yes: OpenComponents (version-exists rejection; registry-side delete a residual Unknown), Zephyr (immutable snapshots), Bit (component versions). Conditional: import maps (immutability is convention, not enforced). No: same-URL strategies (nothing retained). Prerequisite for governance.rollback but deliberately split (retention vs repoint vs delete).

attributes.question: Does keeping consumers on the intended participant version rely on operator-managed cache-busting or short TTLs of a mutable well-known URL, rather than immutable content-addressed URLs or a versioned pointer?
attributes.notes: Yes: MF (remoteEntry and manifest URLs, community-convention finding), web components (URL versioning convention), same-URL child entries (qiankun, wujie, micro-app, iframe documents). No: Zephyr (content-addressed snapshots), import maps (immutable versioned artifact URLs), OC (versioned registry paths).

attributes.question: Do participants deploy as static artifacts servable by any static file host or CDN, as opposed to running HTTP services?
attributes.notes: Yes: MF, Native Federation, import maps, single-spa, web components, iframe and hyperfrontend feature apps, qiankun, wujie, micro-app children. No: Podium podlets, OC components with server logic, SSR fragment services, Multi-Zones apps. Conditional: edge-side fragments (static fragment HTML possible, services common). Splits client-composition from server-composition families.

attributes.question: Must a strategy-specific server or service (registry, feed, gateway, composition proxy, router, layout tier) be deployed and operated in the production request path, beyond static file hosting?
attributes.notes: Absorbs runtime.shared-service-critical-path and operations.selfop-central-service (who operates it: self-host vs managed noted per unit; vendor dependence is hosting.control-plane). Yes: OC registry (plus storage, optional DB), web-fragments gateway, Multi-Zones router, reverse-proxy tier, ESI and edge composer, Cloudflare router worker, ILC, podium layout servers. Conditional: Piral (feed at boot is the standard model; self-host sample, buy cloud, or static pilet list), zephyr (resolution layer), reverse-proxy (self-host vs managed). No: MF, NF CSR, single-spa, qiankun, import maps, iframes, hyperfrontend (hf serve optional), web components (static origins only).

attributes.question: Does the solution define or ship a first-party runtime discovery artifact or service (manifest, feed, registry, routing map) that the host consults to resolve participants?
attributes.notes: Yes: MF 2.0 mf-manifest.json, NF federation.manifest.json, Piral feed spec, OC registry, Picard (Piral plus MFEWG schemas), Podium manifest, Zephyr, import maps (the map itself), Vercel microfrontends.json. No: raw iframes, web components (gap by design), qiankun, wujie, micro-app (code registration), hyperfrontend (metadata format exists, no registry today). NA: islands (nothing to discover).

attributes.question: Must all participants be served to end users under a single public origin or domain (path-split or proxied) for the strategy to function?
attributes.notes: Yes: Multi-Zones, reverse-proxy route composition (subdomain variant conditional), Cloudflare Workers MFE, server and edge fragment composition (one composed origin). No: iframes, hyperfrontend, MF, NF, import maps, web components (any origin, subject to CORS). Domain-topology axis; also drives cookie and session findings elsewhere.

attributes.question: When a participant is hosted on a different origin than the host page, must the participant origin serve CORS headers for loading to work?
attributes.notes: Yes: qiankun, wujie, micro-app (host-side fetch), NF and import maps (module fetches). Conditional: MF (classic script tag exempt; manifest and ESM fetches need CORS). No: iframe and hyperfrontend (frame navigation exempt). NA: proxy and server-composed families (no cross-origin client fetch).

attributes.question: Must participants or their serving infrastructure run on one specific vendor's hosting platform?
attributes.notes: Yes: Cloudflare Workers MFE (all verticals are Workers; hosting captivity split), commercetools Frontend (vendor delivery layer). Conditional: Zephyr (managed default; BYOC moves data plane only). No: Vercel Multi-Zones (self-hostable core; platform features separate), web-fragments (sponsorship, not dependency), all OSS strategies.

attributes.question: What is the lowest level on the migration scale (model/migration.md section 2, ids 1-8) this unit demands of an existing application before first successful participation?
attributes.notes: Value is a scale-level id, not the standard Yes/No vocabulary: the normalization layered over the atoms below (REQ-MATRIX-03). Record per mode where modes differ: Luigi embed-only vs full client, wujie reconstruction vs singleton, micro-app zero-mod marketing vs sandbox tolerance.

attributes.question: What is the lowest migration-scale level this unit demands of the composing or host application as one-time adoption work?
attributes.notes: Scale-level value, not Yes/No; one-time only (recurring per-participant cost is deployment.new-participant-host-change). Forced by the spread: Picard and OC (add script or tag) vs Podium and web-fragments (new tier) vs Piral (instance becomes app root) vs commercial platforms (platform migration).

attributes.question: Must any of the participant application's existing source code be edited before it can participate at all?
attributes.notes: Canonical guidance id (renamed from migration.participant.source-modification-required). No: iframe, reverse-proxy, ESI, wujie reconstruction, Luigi embed-only. Yes: single-spa, qiankun, hyperfrontend (hostee SDK glue). Conditional: micro-app (global-leakage or router-base issues can force edits despite zero-mod marketing).

attributes.question: Must the participant's entry or startup code change (export mount/unmount lifecycles, defer boot, parameterize the mount node) for full participation?
attributes.notes: Level-4 atom. Yes: single-spa, qiankun, Piral pilet setup, Luigi full client, hyperfrontend. Conditional by mode: wujie singleton (__WUJIE_MOUNT), micro-app optional UMD hooks, Luigi (embed-only skips it, degraded). No: iframe, route and proxy composition.

attributes.question: Must application internals change in bounded areas beyond the entry point (routing base or publicPath, mount-path or URL-prefix assumptions, global or DOM exclusivity, style scoping)?
attributes.notes: Level-5 atom. Conditional: Workers router (mount-path-agnostic code), reverse-proxy and multi-zones (prefix-separable URL space), qiankun (publicPath, CORS), micro-app (sandbox tolerance), single-spa (surrender the document shell). No: iframe, ESI fragments.

attributes.question: Must the participant change where or how it is hosted or served (mandated platform, registry publish, new serving infrastructure)?
attributes.notes: Candidate missing level flagged in migration.md section 2. Yes: Cloudflare Workers (every vertical on Workers), Zephyr (managed or orchestrated serving), OC (registry publish), commercial platforms. No: iframe, import maps, web components (any static host).

attributes.question: Starting from a feature inside an existing monolith, must that feature first be extracted into an independently built and deployed unit before it can participate (no in-place wrapping)?
attributes.notes: Level-6 atom. Yes: multi-zones (carve URL boundaries, no runtime shims), MF and NF remotes, Zephyr. No: is-land (in-place progressive enhancement), web-component tag wrap. Conditional: ESI and SSF (region endpoint extraction only).

attributes.question: For an existing application, does adoption amount to level 7-8 work: a framework port, architectural inversion, or wholesale platform and workflow migration?
attributes.notes: Yes: commercial platforms (scaffolded repo, Studio, hub: wholesale, not a layer). Conditional: islands for an existing SPA (server-first inversion), Bit full value (workspace model). No for most. A Yes triggers REQ-Q-04: simpler non-MFE alternatives re-enter.

attributes.question: Can an already-deployed application whose owners will change nothing (build output, exports, and source all untouched) participate through host-side work alone?
attributes.notes: Canonical eliminating-answer guard (migration.md section 5); absorbs framework.unmodified-app-participates (URL-only participation) and buildtime.unmodified-app-participates (build output format unchanged). Yes: Luigi by-URL embed (degraded participation), reverse-proxy, iframe (framing headers are participant-controlled: Conditional), wujie reconstruction mode, web-fragments, multi-zones. Conditional: micro-app (fetchable entry plus CORS are participant-side). No: single-spa (lifecycle adoption), qiankun v2 (UMD exports plus public-path.js plus CORS), MF, Piral, hyperfrontend, web-components (must define an element), all bundler-coupled units.

attributes.question: Can a decades-old application with no reproducible modern build (server-rendered, jQuery-era) participate without first acquiring one (required level at most 2)?
attributes.notes: A broken build caps appetite at level 2 regardless of willingness (migration.md section 8). Yes: iframe (classic strangler entry), proxy, ESI, Podium wrap, web-component tag around a legacy screen. No: MF, NF, import maps (need ESM artifacts).

attributes.question: Can adoption proceed one route, region, or feature at a time while the untouched legacy stays in production (strangler-fig), with no big-bang cutover?
attributes.notes: Near-universal Yes (multi-zones, web-fragments, proxy, ESI, Workers, hyperfrontend) but guards a hard constraint: No for commercial platforms (wholesale adoption). Conditional: islands (cheap for MPA, rewrite for SPA), Piral (shell becomes root first).

attributes.question: Does adoption require standing up or controlling a new infrastructure tier in front of or beside the existing site (proxy or CDN contract, gateway middleware, layout server, component registry)?
attributes.notes: Capability precondition that blocks teams without infra control (ESI, reverse-proxy dossiers). Yes: reverse-proxy, ESI (capable CDN or proxy tier), Podium layout tier, web-fragments gateway, OC registry plus storage. No: client-side composition (single-spa, MF, web components, wujie). Steady-state operation of the tier is deployment.strategy-service-in-path.

attributes.question: Must the composing application be re-rooted under the unit's shell or root config (host gives up ownership of its document shell or application root)?
attributes.notes: Yes: single-spa root config, Piral standard path (instance is the application root). Conditional: Piral as embedded library (possible-extension), Luigi container mode (avoids rehosting under Core). No: OC tag, Picard script add, web-components per-tag, iframe.

attributes.question: After adoption, do participants remain standalone runnable and deployable applications outside the composition (bounded exit, low cost.evolve)?
attributes.notes: Transitional-architecture viability atom. Yes: wujie and micro-app (HTML-entry children), multi-zones, iframe. No: Piral pilets (plain libraries), single-spa apps that surrendered their HTML entry. Conditional: MF remotes (need a standalone build mode).

attributes.question: Is there an officially documented migration path into this unit from an incumbent composition format (webpack MF, SystemJS/single-spa, a prior major)?
attributes.notes: Yes: NF from MF (import-path swap, side-by-side mode), import maps from SystemJS. Conditional: Picard and Piral mf schema (host foreign formats), import maps from MF (via NF only). No: single-spa's promised SystemJS-to-ESM guide has not shipped.

attributes.question: Does the currently adoptable line carry a known forced breaking migration ahead (announced EOL, breaking next major, format deprecation)?
attributes.notes: Yes: qiankun v2 to v3 rearchitecture (v3 still RC), nextjs-mf EOL, originjs Vite plugin to official runtime. Conditional: NF v3 to v4 (guided, bridge package), single-spa SystemJS estates (path exists, guide absent). No: browser-primitive units (iframe, import maps, web components).

attributes.question: Is there documented vendor guidance or multi-year production-adopter evidence supporting the unit as the permanent architecture, rather than solely migration scaffolding?
attributes.notes: Decidability: tightened from a judgment call to documented evidence; the REQ-STATE-09 robustness test depends on it. Most Yes. No or Conditional where evidence forces exit: Picard dormancy risk, qiankun v2 (pending v3), graveyard units. Distinct from forced-remigration-pending: asks whether staying indefinitely is supportable.

attributes.question: Does the unit's own documentation explicitly endorse use by a single coordinated team on one release train, rather than redirecting that case to simpler tooling?
attributes.notes: Renamed from ownership.serves-single-team. Decidability: score only explicit documentation statements. Yes: non-MFE baselines, islands (design center). No: hyperfrontend (self-conceded, you probably do not need it). Guards the REQ-Q-04 no-MFE outcome.

attributes.question: Can a team hold enforceable review and ownership authority over its participant's source (separate repo, or path ownership with required review)?
attributes.notes: Near-universal Yes (CODEOWNERS covers monorepo baselines). Kept as anchor of the mandated three-way team-ownership split so baselines never score ambiguously against MFEs.

attributes.question: Does the owning team control when its participant's changes reach production users, independent of any shared release train?
attributes.notes: No: all non-MFE baselines, islands, bit (consumer rebuild gates visibility). Yes: runtime-composed families. Second member of the team-ownership split; deployment.host-rebuild-required owns the rebuild mechanics, this row records the ownership role.

attributes.question: Does the owning team operate its participant as its own running service or origin in production (its own on-call surface)?
attributes.notes: Yes: podium and server-side fragment services, edge fragments, multi-zones, reverse-proxy zones. No: static-artifact participants executed by the host runtime (MF remotes, pilets, packages, islands). Third member of the team-ownership split.

attributes.question: Can a participant owned by a separate organization be composed via surfaces it already exposes (URL, script tag, published artifact) while treated as a distinct security principal?
attributes.notes: Canonical guidance id (renamed from ownership.serves-external-participant). Yes: iframe (strongest, browser-enforced), hyperfrontend (claimed). No: server-side fragments (explicitly trusted-only), shared-realm families. Boundary-strength decomposition lives in the security group.

attributes.question: Can the participant run inside a host page whose owner makes at most one minimal documented change (one tag, URL, or script), adopting no build tool or framework?
attributes.notes: Renamed from ownership.serves-unmodifiable-host to align the guidance id. Yes: hyperfrontend (design center), iframes, web-components. No: single-spa, piral, multi-zones, where the host must be the unit's own shell or router. Aligns the white-label topology.

attributes.question: Can a participant deploy on a schedule other teams neither know nor approve, with no first-party mechanism erroring or requiring a freeze, train, or synchronized rollout on the resulting skew?
attributes.notes: Renamed from ownership.serves-distrusted-cadence; decidability tightened to mechanical skew behavior. Conditional: module-federation and native-federation (singleton plus strictVersion errors on skew; governance required). Yes: iframes, import-map scopes; bit passes via consumer pinning (insulation, not runtime tolerance).

attributes.question: Can participants run mutually incompatible versions of shared dependencies (including framework majors) indefinitely, with no cross-team upgrade train ever forced by default configuration?
attributes.notes: Renamed from ownership.serves-uncoordinated-upgrades; absorbs framework.default-version-lockstep (inverted) and migration.participant.framework-alignment-forced (inverted). Yes: import-maps (scoped side-by-side), iframes, reverse-proxy, hyperfrontend. No or Conditional: MF and native-federation under default singleton plus strictVersion (coordinated major upgrades remain necessary; NF couples framework majors), Piral (shell-owned importmap), single-build units (islands, baselines, modular monolith: no staggered majors as peers).

attributes.question: Can a new participant team join the composition without any action by the central artifact's owner (e.g. publish-to-registry or feed discovery)?
attributes.notes: Asks whose action, not what rebuilds (deployment.new-participant-host-change owns that). Yes: piral feed, opencomponents registry, zephyr. No: single-spa root config, podium (layout code change), web-fragments (gateway registry), qiankun. Conditional: luigi (adopter-built aggregation), server-side fragments (registry-based only).

attributes.question: Does effective operation require a standing platform-owner role distinct from product teams (shell, router, layout, registry, or CDN and edge-config owner)?
attributes.notes: Yes: piral, luigi, podium, cloudflare router, reverse-proxy routing tier, edge-side (CDN-config owner is a deployment gatekeeper: strongest form). No: hyperfrontend (claimed), plain iframes, web-components contract.

attributes.question: Can non-developers hold page-composition authority (which participants appear where) through a supported UI?
attributes.notes: Yes only in commercial platforms (Studio's developer vs business-user role split); forced by commercial-platform-illustrations. Nearly all engineering units No; keeps that product class from falsely scoring as team-topology MFE.

attributes.question: Is the participant's shipped code guaranteed to execute as shipped, with no host-side rewriting of its HTML, JS, or CSS?
attributes.notes: No: wujie (replace and plugins rewrite at injection; a trust-topology fact), micro-app (plugin code patching). Yes: iframes, module-federation. Decisive for vendor and white-label seats where the participant owner must vouch for its bytes.

attributes.question: Can a participant simultaneously act as a host composing its own participants (chained ownership)?
attributes.notes: Yes: wujie (nested keep-alive documented), iframes, module-federation (hosts can be remotes). Unknown for many units; record Unknown honestly. Aligns the B2B-distribution topology where the middle party is participant-owner and host-owner at once.

attributes.question: Is the unit's composition boundary another project's contract, so it inherits that project's lifetime (the Ara-on-Hypernova pattern)?
attributes.notes: Yes: picard (interop over MF, NF, pilet formats), toolchain-branded wrappers (brands over module-federation), zephyr (serves the MF ecosystem). No: primaries defining their own boundary. From graveyard-illustrations' ownership finding.

attributes.question: Does avoiding duplicated, conflicting, or broken shared dependencies require standing cross-team version governance (agreed names, ranges, singleton policy, upgrade trains) before and after builds?
attributes.notes: Canonical guidance id (renamed from operations.shared-dep-governance-required); absorbs buildtime.dep-agreement-before-build. Yes: MF (share-scope governance, documented skew and double-React), NF (singleton plus strictVersion couples framework majors), Piral (shell-owned importmap and dep policy), import-maps (bare-specifier naming plus externals), single-spa (externals convention). Conditional: import maps with scopes (divergence without lockstep). No or NA: iframes, proxy, zones, multi-zones, podium, hyperfrontend, wujie, qiankun, cloudflare-workers, web-fragments, islands (no runtime sharing; duplication cost is a performance-group question).

attributes.question: Does the unit ship machinery for host-participant version-skew moments (deploy-skew fallback routing, semver renegotiation, manifest polling and refresh, runtime handshake version gate)?
attributes.notes: Yes: Vercel (skew fallbacks, platform-only), Podium (manifest polling, retries, timeouts), HyperFrontend (handshake version gate), MF (semver negotiation; silent double-load caveat). No: raw iframes (uncoordinated releases silently break the message contract), WC, single-spa core. Conditional where platform-tier-only. The pure connect-time gate is contracts.connect-compat-gate.

attributes.question: Do a participant's runtime errors and stack traces surface directly in the host document's error stream (same realm), rather than staying behind the composition boundary?
attributes.notes: Yes: shared-realm units (MF, NF, single-spa, Piral, WC, islands, qiankun). No: cross-origin iframes and HyperFrontend (window.onerror does not cross; browser-guarantee) and server and edge composition (failures live in server logs). No forces in-participant reporting.

attributes.question: Does the unit ship a mechanism that attributes a runtime failure to the owning participant (per-unit error boundary, liveness state, or per-fragment fallback-serve signal) without adopter-built tagging?
attributes.notes: Yes: Piral (per-component containment), Podium and SSI (fallbacks), HyperFrontend (typed relationship failures). No: web components (deliberate per-team tagging required), MF, import maps. Conditional: single-spa (lifecycle-phase only, SKIP_BECAUSE_BROKEN). Distinct from containment (isolation group): this is who gets paged.

attributes.question: Does correlating one user journey across the composition boundary require adopter-implemented correlation IDs because no shared runtime context spans the boundary?
attributes.notes: Yes: reverse-proxy (correlation discipline), multi-zones, iframes, HyperFrontend, edge and server composition (multi-tier logs). No: shared-realm units (one APM agent sees the whole page). NA: single-deploy baselines and islands (nothing to correlate across).

attributes.question: Can an operator enumerate which participant versions are live per environment through a first-party surface (dashboard, registry, manifest, or the map itself)?
attributes.notes: Yes: Zephyr (Mission Control), OC registry, import-map family (the map is the inventory), multi-zones dashboard. No: raw MF (what-is-deployed-where is adopter-built or third-party: the MF-vs-Zephyr fight), WC. Keep distinct from runtime telemetry (governance.usage-monitoring).

attributes.question: Does a first-party runtime debugging surface exist for the composition (browser devtools extension or built-in debug UI)?
attributes.notes: Yes: MF (Chrome DevTools), micro-app (chrome plugin), Native Federation (read-only panel), Zephyr (Chromium-only extension), HyperFrontend (hf dev). Conditional: single-spa (import-map-overrides is ecosystem lineage, not platform). No: most server, edge, iframe, WC units.

attributes.question: Does first-party tooling run the fully composed experience on a developer machine (dev proxy, shell emulator, local registry or dev mode)?
attributes.notes: Yes: multi-zones (microfrontends proxy), Piral (pilet debug plus kras mocking), OC (local:true), HyperFrontend. Conditional: import maps (ecosystem overrides tooling). No: edge-side, its stated weakest operational point.

attributes.question: Can the production composition mechanism itself execute on a developer laptop without vendor infrastructure or simulators (dev-prod parity of the composition tier)?
attributes.notes: No: edge-side (Varnish and CDN PoP require containers or vendor simulators). Conditional: Cloudflare VMFE (wrangler-local), Vercel (OSS rewrites yes; platform skew and preview routing no). Yes: browser-composed and Node-composed families.

attributes.question: Can a participant be developed and run standalone, without the host or composer running, via a documented mechanism (mocked context defaults, emulator package)?
attributes.notes: Yes: Podium (.defaults() context), Piral (emulator), qiankun and micro-app sub-apps, iframes and zones (normal apps). Conditional: MF remotes (authoring choice), Luigi (embed-only degrades: no routing, context, UX services).

attributes.question: Does the unit ship first-party utilities for testing the composed system (integration and e2e helpers, routing validation, emulator-backed tests)?
attributes.notes: Yes: multi-zones (validateRouting, middleware test utils, published JSON schema), Cloudflare VMFE (vitest-pool-workers integration tests). Conditional: Piral (emulator plus kras). No: nearly all others; the e2e story is an evidence gap across dossiers, not parity.

attributes.question: Does anything verify at build or deploy time that a participant still satisfies its consumers' contracts (beyond editor-time type hints)?
attributes.notes: No: MF (explicit split: d.ts hinting yes, deploy-time enforcement no; types can lag runtime). Unknown: Zephyr (rollback compatibility check unevidenced). Conditional: Bit (Ripple rebuilds dependents, cloud-only), HyperFrontend (build-time downgrade signal only), multi-zones (routing schema only).

attributes.question: Is maintenance concentrated in a single company or single dominant individual, such that losing that one sponsor plausibly stalls the project?
attributes.notes: Absorbs ownership.solution-sponsor-diversity (inverted). Yes: wujie (Tencent, one maintainer, prior stall), micro-app (JD), qiankun (Ant), MF (ByteDance plus one lead), Luigi (SAP), HyperFrontend (one maintainer; dossier says must not be softened), web-fragments (Cloudflare-sponsored), picard, Hypernova pattern (archive tied to sponsor exit). No: browser-standard strategies (iframes, WC, import maps: multi-vendor platform).

attributes.question: Does official documentation define two or more configuration modes or version lines that change this unit's answers to isolation or runtime attributes, requiring it to be scored as distinct configurations?
attributes.notes: Decidability: tightened to documented modes that flip other cells. Yes: micro-app (with vs iframe sandbox), qiankun (v2 vs v3-RC, Proxy vs snapshot), wujie (three run modes plus degrade tier), Luigi (iframe vs WC). No: single-config units. A concrete cognitive-overhead cause; four dossiers requested per-mode scoring.
